{"id": "53504bbf-e545-4854-8c52-1cb5c8c51222", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_UVTol744v27QLHYxdEec3L", "content": "[{'text': '# kubectl discovery \u2014 core areas 1\u201327\\n\\nRun every command through the AWS DevOps Agent MCP tool **`use_kubectl`**. Every code span below is one separate tool invocation; never combine commands with shell operators. Allowed operations: `get`, `describe`, `logs`, `version`, `config current-context`, `cluster-info`, `top`, and `get --raw`. Tool results remain transient in conversation and must not be written to Amazon S3 or a file. Record command, scope, timestamp, and resourceVersion where available in the transient ledger. Continue with [`kubectl-discovery-commands-deep-dive.md`](kubectl-discovery-commands-deep-dive.md); fleet/payload detail is in the *Scaling guidance (large clusters)* section at the end of this file.\\n\\n## Fetch and projection rules\\n\\nProduce the reusable fetch IDs named by [`runtime/discovery-manifest.md`](runtime/discovery-manifest.md). Cache only for the confirmed cluster/context/scope, project immediately to bounded evidence, reuse only for listed dependent areas, then drop raw JSON. A dependent area is attempted only after its extraction runs. At 500+ pods never create `POD_JSON`; use namespace batches, field selectors, custom columns, and bounded `POD_PROJECTION_`. CRD-specific NotFound checks are always separate from `CRD_JSON`. Secret data is never fetched.\\n\\n| Area / fetch | Separate read-only calls | Required bounded extraction |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| 1 CLUSTER_INFO | `kubectl version -o json`
`kubectl config current-context`
`kubectl cluster-info` | identity, server/client version, context; stop on mismatch. |\\n| 2 NODES / `NODE_JSON` | `kubectl get nodes -o json` | count; Ready/Disk/Memory/PID pressure; allocatable; providerID; labels, taints, AZ, OS, arch, capacity type, accelerators, compute type. A wide projection is derived locally. |\\n| 3 NAMESPACES / `NS_JSON` | `kubectl get namespaces -o json` | count, labels, PSS/tenant hints. |\\n| 4 DEPLOYMENTS / `DEPLOY_JSON` | `kubectl get deployments -A -o json` | replicas/status, strategy/history, images, resources, probes, SA, scheduling, lifecycle; scope/sample per scale rules. |\\n| 5 STATEFULSETS / `STS_JSON` | `kubectl get statefulsets -A -o json` | replicas/status, update strategy, PVC templates, probes, grace/minReadySeconds. |\\n| 6 DAEMONSETS / `DS_JSON` | `kubectl get daemonsets -A -o json` | rollout/placement/resources; device/CSI/host-agent detection. |\\n| 7 PODS / `POD_JSON` or scoped projections | `kubectl get pods -A -o json` only below payload guard
`kubectl get pods -A --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -o name`
`kubectl get pods -A --field-selector=status.phase=Failed -o name` | total/phase, CrashLoop/ImagePull/OOM/restarts, images, resources, probes, SA, security, QoS, scheduling, lifecycle; describe only bounded problem samples. At guard, obtain total from bounded namespace/name projections instead of cluster JSON. |\\n| 8 SERVICES / `SVC_JSON` | `kubectl get services -A -o json` | count/type distribution, selectors, LB metadata/target hints. |\\n| 9 ENDPOINTS | `kubectl get endpoints -A -o wide`
`kubectl get endpointslices -A -o wide` | empty endpoints, EndpointSlice adoption, bounded counts. |\\n| 10 INGRESS / `INGRESS_JSON` | `kubectl get ingressclasses -o wide`
`kubectl get ingress -A -o json` | count/classes/annotations/status; detect controllers from bounded pod projection; Gateway API stays area 40. |\\n| 11 HPA / `HPA_JSON` | `kubectl get hpa -A -o json` | count, min/max/current, targets/conditions; autoscaling feature. |\\n| 12 VPA | `kubectl get vpa -A -o wide` | CRD-specific presence/count/mode; NotFound = feature false. |\\n| 13 KEDA | `kubectl get scaledobjects -A -o wide`
`kubectl get triggerauthentications -A -o wide` | feature/counts/auth scope; each CRD probe remains separate. |\\n| 14 PDB / `PDB_JSON` | `kubectl get poddisruptionbudgets -A -o json` | count/selectors/allowed disruptions; blocking and workload coverage inputs. |\\n| 15 JOBS | `kubectl get jobs -A -o wide` | count, failed/active/completion summary. |\\n| 16 CRONJOBS | `kubectl get cronjobs -A -o wide` | count, schedules/suspension/history. |\\n| 17 CONFIGMAPS | `kubectl get configmaps -A -o wide` | metadata-only count; content only for explicitly named non-sensitive kube-system configs. |\\n| 18 SECRETS | `kubectl get secrets -A -o custom-columns=NAMESPACE:.metadata.namespace,NAME:.metadata.name,TYPE:.type,AGE:.metadata.creationTimestamp` | metadata/type count only; never JSON/YAML/data. Helm-manifest inspection is separate gated upgrade work with explicit handling. |\\n| 19 EVENTS | `kubectl get events -A --field-selector type=Warning --sort-by=.lastTimestamp` | bounded recent warning reasons/resources/timestamps. |\\n| 20 STORAGE / `SC_JSON`,`PV_JSON` | `kubectl get storageclasses -o json`
`kubectl get pv -o json`
`kubectl get pvc -A -o wide` | counts/provisioners/gp2-gp3/CSI, binding mode, encryption/KMS, PV/PVC state/AZ. Derive `storageclasses_immediate_binding` and `storageclasses_unencrypted`. |\\n| 21 NETWORKPOLICIES / `NP_JSON` | `kubectl get networkpolicies -A -o json` | count, namespace/default-deny coverage, selectors/types. |\\n| 22 RBAC / `RBAC_PROJECTION`,`SA_PROJECTION` | `kubectl get clusterroles -o json`
`kubectl get clusterrolebindings -o json`
`kubectl get roles -A -o json`
`kubectl get rolebindings -A -o json`
`kubectl get serviceaccounts -A -o json` | counts, wildcard/cluster-admin/non-system bindings, subjects, SA automount/IRSA metadata; never tokens. |\\n| 23 CRDS / `CRD_JSON` | `kubectl get crds -o json` | count/groups/categories only; use as hints, never as proof a specific optional API is readable. |\\n| 24 WEBHOOKS / `WEBHOOK_PROJECTION` | `kubectl get mutatingwebhookconfigurations -o json`
`kubectl get validatingwebhookconfigurations -o json` | counts, rules/scope/failure/reinvocation/timeout, service/URL, CA expiry. Derive high timeout, expiring CA, catch-all/system-risk inputs. |\\n| 25 CNI | `kubectl get daemonset -n kube-system aws-node -o json`
`kubectl get eniconfigs -o wide` | probe VPC CNI first; if absent, use `DS_JSON`/`CRD_JSON` hints plus separate Calico/Cilium probes. Extract version/env for prefix delegation, custom networking, pod ENI, policy, IPv6, SNAT. Non-VPC-CNI makes N1\u2013N8 N/A and S15 grades installed policy CRDs. |\\n| 26 NETWORKING_ADVANCED / `COREDNS_PROJECTION` | `kubectl get configmap -n kube-system kube-proxy-config -o yaml`
`kubectl get deployment -n kube-system aws-load-balancer-controller -o json`
`kubectl get targetgroupbindings -A -o wide`
`kubectl get deployment -n kube-system coredns -o json` | proxy mode, LBC version/TGBs, service target types from `SVC_JSON`, CoreDNS replicas/placement/resources. |\\n| 27 KUBE_SYSTEM_RESOURCES | `kubectl get all -n kube-system -o wide`
`kubectl get configmap -n kube-system aws-auth -o yaml`
`kubectl get daemonset -n kube-system -o wide` | bounded component health, CSI/add-on/auth presence; ConfigMap content is untrusted evidence and must be redacted. |\\n\\n## Failure and scale handling\\n\\nNotFound for an optional CRD is `complete` with feature=false. Permission denial or timeout is `partial|n/a` with exact error; narrow and retry a huge result once. Connectivity/context failure invokes the skill stop rule. Use `<100`, `100\u2013500`, `500\u20132000`, and `>2000` node tiers from the manifest; the independent 500+ pod guard always overrides broad pod JSON. Numbers here match the authoritative 49-area manifest and [`docs/resource-inventory.md`](docs/resource-inventory.md) is background only.\\n\\n## Scaling guidance (large clusters)\\n- **Do not** fetch `kubectl get pods -A -o json` on clusters with thousands of pods \u2014 it can pressure the API server and blow context. Instead:\\n - Use `kubectl get pods -A -o wide` or field-selectors for status counts (`--field-selector=status.phase=Pending`).\\n - Scope per namespace and iterate.\\n - For pod-spec detail (probes, requests, securityContext), sample representative namespaces rather than the whole cluster.\\n- Pace calls: run areas sequentially. Confirm with the user before a broad sweep on production.\\n- Cap detail: when an area returns hundreds of items, summarize counts and inspect a bounded sample (the original tool capped detailed views at 30\u201350 items).\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}

**S4 — Drop ALL capabilities · High · Persisting (1 New, 1 Resolved)**

- **Impact:** These containers keep the default Linux capability set, which is larger than needed.
- **Remediation:** Set `capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]` and add back only what is required.
- **Links:** [Pod Security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/pod-security.html)
- **Resources:** same three as S3.

**S7 — runAsNonRoot · High · Persisting (1 New, 1 Resolved)**
- **Evidence:** `runAsNonRoot` is unset on the same three workloads. The runtime user is uid 65535 only because of the image. Nothing enforces it.
- **Impact:** A different image or tag could run as root without being blocked.
- **Remediation:** Set `runAsNonRoot: true` and a concrete `runAsUser`.
- **Links:** [Pod Security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/pod-security.html)
- **Resources:** same three as S3.

**S9 — Pod Security Admission · Medium · Persisting**
- **Evidence:** `default` and `team-a` have only the `kubernetes.io/metadata.name` label. `secure-ns` has `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted`.
- **Impact:** This is why `hostnet-pod` was admitted. The same pod spec would be rejected in `secure-ns`.
- **Remediation:** Add `enforce: baseline` and `warn: restricted` labels to `default` and `team-a`.
- **Links:** [Pod Security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/pod-security.html) · [Kubernetes PSA labels](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/enforce-standards-namespace-labels/)
- **Resources:** `Namespace/default`; `Namespace/team-a`

**S5 — seccomp RuntimeDefault · Medium · Persisting (1 New, 1 Resolved)**
- **Evidence:** No `seccompProfile` on the same three workloads. `hardened-app` sets `RuntimeDefault`.
- **Impact:** These containers run without syscall filtering.
- **Remediation:** Set `seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault` at pod level.
- **Links:** [Runtime Security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/runtime-security.html)
- **Resources:** same three as S3.

**S6 — readOnlyRootFilesystem · Medium · Persisting (1 New, 1 Resolved)**
- **Evidence:** Unset on the same three workloads. `hardened-app` and `coredns` set it true.
- **Impact:** An attacker inside the container can write binaries and change files.
- **Remediation:** Set `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`, with `emptyDir` mounts for any paths that must be writable.
- **Links:** [Pod Security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/pod-security.html)
- **Resources:** same three as S3.

**S14 — automountServiceAccountToken · Medium · Persisting (1 New, 1 Resolved)**
- **Evidence:** `legacy-web`, `env-secret-app` and `hostnet-pod` all use the `default` SA with the token unset, so each mounts a projected `kube-api-access-*` token volume. `hardened-app` sets `automountServiceAccountToken: false`. All three run the `pause` image, which makes no API calls.
- **Impact:** A compromised pod would hold a free Kubernetes API credential.
- **Remediation:** Set `automountServiceAccountToken: false` on the SA or the pod.
- **Links:** [Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/identity-and-access-management.html)
- **Resources:** same three as S3.

**S12 — Access Entries / API auth mode · Medium · Persisting**
- **Evidence:** `kube-system/aws-auth` exists with a `mapRoles` entry for the node role, and `authenticationMode` is `API_AND_CONFIG_MAP`. There are 9 access entries. I listed them but did not check their policies (AX2 is outside this unit).
- **Impact:** The deprecated ConfigMap remains a second, less auditable access path.
- **Remediation:** Move principals to Access Entries and switch the mode to `API`. The node role's entry is the one most likely to need care.
- **Links:** [Cluster Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/cluster-access-management.html)
- **Resource:** `kube-system/ConfigMap/aws-auth`

- **Impact:** Secrets live as plain Kubernetes Secrets. `team-a/env-secret-app` references `app-creds`.
- **Remediation:** Adopt External Secrets Operator or the Secrets Store CSI driver, and pair it with SM1.
- **Links:** [Data encryption and secrets management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/data-encryption-and-secrets-management.html)

- **Remediation:** Enable ECR enhanced scanning (Inspector), or run Trivy or Grype in CI or in-cluster.
- **Links:** [Image Security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/image-security.html) · [ECR image scanning](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-scanning.html)

- **Remediation:** Deploy Kyverno or Gatekeeper, starting in audit mode.
- **Links:** [Pod Security (Policy as Code)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/pod-security.html)

- **Resource:** `vpc-00000000000000001`

**S36 — VPC CNI dedicated IAM role · Medium · Persisting**
- **Evidence:** The `vpc-cni` add-on has `serviceAccountRoleArn: null` and no Pod Identity association. There are 0 Pod Identity associations in the cluster, and the node role carries `AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy`. Reading the `aws-node` ServiceAccount itself was Forbidden.

- **Remediation:** Create a dedicated Pod Identity or IRSA role for `aws-node`, then remove the CNI policy from the node role.
- **Links:** [VPC CNI best practices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/vpc-cni.html)

- **Remediation:** Enable the `audit` log type, and ideally `authenticator`.
- **Links:** [Auditing and Logging](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/auditing-and-logging.html)
- **Resource:** `[redacted ARN]`

- **Impact:** Node disks and any future volumes are unencrypted at rest.
- **Remediation:** Use encrypted launch settings for nodes (or enable EBS default encryption), and fix the StorageClass as in S32.
- **Links:** [Data encryption and secrets management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/data-encryption-and-secrets-management.html)
- **Resources:** `StorageClass/gp2`; `vol-00000000000000001`; `vol-00000000000000002`

**S19 — Secrets via volume, not env · Low · Persisting**
- **Evidence:** `team-a/env-secret-app` has env `DB_PASSWORD` from `secretKeyRef` (`app-creds`, key `password`). I did not read the Secret value.
- **Impact:** Env-var secrets leak more easily through crash dumps and `describe`.
- **Remediation:** Mount the Secret as a read-only volume.
- **Links:** [Data encryption and secrets management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/data-encryption-and-secrets-management.html)

## 4. Detailed findings
All remediations are proposals for human approval. Nothing was changed on the cluster.

**S2 — No host namespaces · Security · High · Regressed**
- **Evidence:** `kubectl get pod -n team-a hostnet-pod -o json` returned `"hostNetwork": true`, `podIP: 10.42.0.64` (identical to the node IP), and creation time 2026-11-17T19:34:27Z. `hostPID` and `hostIPC` are unset everywhere. Other hostNetwork users are `aws-node`, `kube-proxy` and the GuardDuty agent, all AWS-managed system components.
- **Severity rationale:** `team-a` has no PSA labels, so nothing blocked it. IMDSv2 hop-limit 1 (S28) protects only pods on the pod network. A host-network pod shares the node's network stack, so it can reach the metadata endpoint and the node role's credentials. That role carries the three managed node policies (SM7).
- **Impact:** The pod can see node-local ports and traffic and can reach the node's IAM credentials.
- **Remediation:** Set `hostNetwork: false` (or delete the pod) and enforce `baseline` or `restricted` PSA on `team-a` (see S9).
- **Links:** [Pod Security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/pod-security.html)
- **Resource:** `team-a/Pod/hostnet-pod`

**SM3 — Endpoint exposure · High · Persisting**
- **Evidence:** `eks describe-cluster` shows `endpointPublicAccess: true`, `publicAccessCidrs: ["0.0.0.0/0"]`, `endpointPrivateAccess: true`.
- **Severity rationale:** The Kubernetes API is internet-reachable from any address. This is a non-prod test cluster, so I kept the pillar's baseline severity.
- **Impact:** Anyone on the internet can reach the API server. It is protected only by authentication and RBAC.
- **Remediation:** Restrict `publicAccessCidrs` to known egress ranges, or disable public access since private access is already on.
- **Links:** [Cluster Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/cluster-access-management.html)
- **Resource:** `[redacted ARN]`

**S32 — StorageClass encryption · High · Persisting**
- **Evidence:** `kubectl get storageclasses -o json` shows `gp2` with `parameters: {fsType: ext4, type: gp2}` and no `encrypted` key.
- **Severity rationale:** Every PVC that uses this class gets an unencrypted volume. There are no PVs today, so exposure is potential rather than current.
- **Impact:** Silent data-at-rest exposure for future volumes.
- **Remediation:** Create or replace the class with `encrypted: "true"` and a `kmsKeyId`. Observation: it uses the legacy in-tree `kubernetes.io/aws-ebs` provisioner, and no EBS CSI add-on is installed.
- **Links:** [Data encryption and secrets management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/data-encryption-and-secrets-management.html)
- **Resource:** `StorageClass/gp2`

**S3 — allowPrivilegeEscalation=false · High · Persisting (1 New instance, 1 Resolved instance)**
- **Evidence:** `allowPrivilegeEscalation` is unset on `default/legacy-web`, `team-a/env-secret-app` and `team-a/hostnet-pod`. `secure-ns/hardened-app` and `coredns` set it false.
- **Scope note:** I graded user workloads, as the previous review did. `aws-node` and `kube-proxy` also leave it unset; these are AWS-managed.
- **Impact:** A process inside these containers can gain more privileges than its parent.
- **Remediation:** Set `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` and enforce it with PSA `restricted`.
- **Links:** [Pod Security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/pod-security.html)
- **Resources:** `default/Deployment/legacy-web`; `team-a/Deployment/env-secret-app`; `team-a/Pod/hostnet-pod`

**S4 — Drop ALL capabilities · High · Persisting (1 New, 1 Resolved)**
- **Evidence:** No `capabilities.drop` on `legacy-web`, `env-secret-app` or `hostnet-pod`. `hardened-app` and `coredns` drop ALL.
- **Impact:** These containers keep the default Linux capability set, which is larger than needed.
- **Remediation:** Set `capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]` and add back only what is required.
- **Links:** [Pod Security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/pod-security.html)
- **Resources:** same three as S3.

**S7 — runAsNonRoot · High · Persisting (1 New, 1 Resolved)**
- **Evidence:** `runAsNonRoot` is unset on the same three workloads. The runtime user is uid 65535 only because of the image. Nothing enforces it.
- **Impact:** A different image or tag could run as root without being blocked.
- **Remediation:** Set `runAsNonRoot: true` and a concrete `runAsUser`.
- **Links:** [Pod Security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/pod-security.html)
- **Resources:** same three as S3.

**S9 — Pod Security Admission · Medium · Persisting**
- **Evidence:** `default` and `team-a` have only the `kubernetes.io/metadata.name` label. `secure-ns` has `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted`.
- **Impact:** This is why `hostnet-pod` was admitted. The same pod spec would be rejected in `secure-ns`.
- **Remediation:** Add `enforce: baseline` and `warn: restricted` labels to `default` and `team-a`.
- **Links:** [Pod Security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/pod-security.html) · [Kubernetes PSA labels](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/enforce-standards-namespace-labels/)
- **Resources:** `Namespace/default`; `Namespace/team-a`

**S5 — seccomp RuntimeDefault · Medium · Persisting (1 New, 1 Resolved)**
- **Evidence:** No `seccompProfile` on the same three workloads. `hardened-app` sets `RuntimeDefault`.
- **Impact:** These containers run without syscall filtering.
- **Remediation:** Set `seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault` at pod level.
- **Links:** [Runtime Security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/runtime-security.html)
- **Resources:** same three as S3.

**S6 — readOnlyRootFilesystem · Medium · Persisting (1 New, 1 Resolved)**
- **Evidence:** Unset on the same three workloads. `hardened-app` and `coredns` set it true.
- **Impact:** An attacker inside the container can write binaries and change files.
- **Remediation:** Set `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`, with `emptyDir` mounts for any paths that must be writable.
- **Links:** [Pod Security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/pod-security.html)
- **Resources:** same three as S3.

**S14 — automountServiceAccountToken · Medium · Persisting (1 New, 1 Resolved)**
- **Evidence:** `legacy-web`, `env-secret-app` and `hostnet-pod` all use the `default` SA with the token unset, so each mounts a projected `kube-api-access-*` token volume. `hardened-app` sets `automountServiceAccountToken: false`. All three run the `pause` image, which makes no API calls.
- **Impact:** A compromised pod would hold a free Kubernetes API credential.
- **Remediation:** Set `automountServiceAccountToken: false` on the SA or the pod.
- **Links:** [Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/identity-and-access-management.html)
- **Resources:** same three as S3.

**S12 — Access Entries / API auth mode · Medium · Persisting**
- **Evidence:** `kube-system/aws-auth` exists with a `mapRoles` entry for the node role, and `authenticationMode` is `API_AND_CONFIG_MAP`. There are 9 access entries. I listed them but did not check their policies (AX2 is outside this unit).
- **Impact:** The deprecated ConfigMap remains a second, less auditable access path.
- **Remediation:** Move principals to Access Entries and switch the mode to `API`. The node role's entry is the one most likely to need care.
- **Links:** [Cluster Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/cluster-access-management.html)
- **Resource:** `kube-system/ConfigMap/aws-auth`

**S18 — External secrets management · Medium · Persisting**
- **Evidence:** The `externalsecrets.external-secrets.io` and `secretproviderclasses` resource types are not served. There is no secrets-store-csi-driver DaemonSet, and none of the 12 pods is a secrets controller.
- **Impact:** Secrets live as plain Kubernetes Secrets. `team-a/env-secret-app` references `app-creds`.
- **Remediation:** Adopt External Secrets Operator or the Secrets Store CSI driver, and pair it with SM1.
- **Links:** [Data encryption and secrets management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/data-encryption-and-secrets-management.html)
- **Resource:** `[redacted ARN]`

**S21 — Image scanning · Medium · Persisting**
- **Evidence:** No scanner among the 12 pods. `ecr:GetRegistryScanningConfiguration` and `inspector2:BatchGetAccountStatus` were both AccessDenied, so registry-side scanning is unverified.
- **Impact:** No scanning signal exists for workload images.
- **Remediation:** Enable ECR enhanced scanning (Inspector), or run Trivy or Grype in CI or in-cluster.
- **Links:** [Image Security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/image-security.html) · [ECR image scanning](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-scanning.html)
- **Resource:** `[redacted ARN]`

**S23 — Policy enforcement engine · Medium · Persisting**
- **Evidence:** `clusterpolicies` (Kyverno) and `constraints` (Gatekeeper) are not served, and no such pods exist. Webhook configurations are unreadable (Forbidden), so confidence is Medium. PSA `restricted` covers only `secure-ns`, so the "PSA alone is enough" N/A exception does not apply.
- **Impact:** Nothing enforces organisation rules at admission outside `secure-ns`.
- **Remediation:** Deploy Kyverno or Gatekeeper, starting in audit mode.
- **Links:** [Pod Security (Policy as Code)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/pod-security.html)
- **Resource:** `[redacted ARN]`

**S30 — VPC flow logs · Medium · Persisting**
- **Evidence:** `ec2 describe-flow-logs` for `vpc-00000000000000001` and both cluster subnets returned `FlowLogs: []`.
- **Impact:** There is no network forensic record for the cluster VPC.
- **Remediation:** Enable VPC-level flow logs to CloudWatch Logs or S3.
- **Links:** [VPC flow logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs.html)
- **Resource:** `vpc-00000000000000001`

**S36 — VPC CNI dedicated IAM role · Medium · Persisting**
- **Evidence:** The `vpc-cni` add-on has `serviceAccountRoleArn: null` and no Pod Identity association. There are 0 Pod Identity associations in the cluster, and the node role carries `AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy`. Reading the `aws-node` ServiceAccount itself was Forbidden.
- **Impact:** CNI permissions ride on the shared node role, which any pod able to reach IMDS can use. That includes host-network pods (S2).
- **Remediation:** Create a dedicated Pod Identity or IRSA role for `aws-node`, then remove the CNI policy from the node role.
- **Links:** [VPC CNI best practices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/vpc-cni.html)
- **Resource:** `kube-system/ServiceAccount/aws-node`

**SM1 — KMS envelope encryption · Medium · Persisting**
- **Evidence:** `describe-cluster` returns no `encryptionConfig`.
- **Impact:** Kubernetes Secrets have no customer-managed envelope encryption.
- **Remediation:** Associate an encryption config with a customer-managed KMS key.
- **Links:** [Data encryption and secrets management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/data-encryption-and-secrets-management.html)
- **Resource:** `[redacted ARN]`

**SM2 — Audit logging · Medium · Persisting**
- **Evidence:** `logging.clusterLogging` has `api` enabled; `audit`, `authenticator`, `controllerManager` and `scheduler` are disabled.
- **Impact:** There is no API audit trail. Investigating incidents such as the hostnet-pod creation is not possible from audit logs.
- **Remediation:** Enable the `audit` log type, and ideally `authenticator`.
- **Links:** [Auditing and Logging](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/auditing-and-logging.html)
- **Resource:** `[redacted ARN]`

**SM4 — EBS/EFS encryption at rest · Medium · Persisting (matched via placeholders)**
- **Evidence:** `gp2` has no `encrypted` parameter. `vol-00000000000000001` and `vol-00000000000000002` (the two gp3 node root volumes) both show `Encrypted: false`. No EFS file systems exist.
- **Impact:** Node disks and any future volumes are unencrypted at rest.
- **Remediation:** Use encrypted launch settings for nodes (or enable EBS default encryption), and fix the StorageClass as in S32.
- **Links:** [Data encryption and secrets management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/data-encryption-and-secrets-management.html)
- **Resources:** `StorageClass/gp2`; `vol-00000000000000001`; `vol-00000000000000002`

**S19 — Secrets via volume, not env · Low · Persisting**
- **Evidence:** `team-a/env-secret-app` has env `DB_PASSWORD` from `secretKeyRef` (`app-creds`, key `password`). I did not read the Secret value.
- **Impact:** Env-var secrets leak more easily through crash dumps and `describe`.
- **Remediation:** Mount the Secret as a read-only volume.
- **Links:** [Data encryption and secrets management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/data-encryption-and-secrets-management.html)
- **Resource:** `team-a/Deployment/env-secret-app`
